title: Quarter Bridge Plan: VPC & On-Prem Governance, Capacity, and OKR Mapping
creator: Sophie Chen
description: Create a concrete quarter-long operational plan that bridges roadmap milestones with governance controls, capacity forecasting, and OKR-aligned initiatives for VPC and on-prem enterprise deliveries. This document coordinates feature roll waves, upgrade windows, and acceptance criteria so sales, SRE, and engineering can commit capacity and runbooks.
background: Customers in regulated verticals have requested clearer upgrade guarantees, capacity commitments, and governance controls for Private (VPC/on-prem) installs. Recent Dedicated customers experienced two upgrade-related incidents last quarter due to mismatched maintenance windows and unexpected capacity spikes. This plan synthesizes learnings into a repeatable quarter bridge for upcoming wave deliveries.
goals: Define three rollout waves with clear acceptance gates and SLOs for 2025-Q2 Private deliveries
Establish governance checklist (RBAC, audit logging, KMS handoff) required before customer onboarding
Produce capacity forecast templates and autoscaling knobs for Dedicated pools that map to expected customer queues
Map each roadmap item to OKRs and measurable signals for product/ops owners
milestones: Milestone B: Capacity forecast model validated with two pilot customers — 2025-03-28
Milestone C: Wave 1 rollout (10 pilot customers) — 2025-04-15
Milestone D: Wave 2 rollout (regional expansion + 25 customers) — 2025-05-15
Milestone E: Post-roll evaluation & OKR signal handoff — 2025-05-30
milestone_details: Governance checklist includes: RBAC templates, audit log retention policy, KMS integration matrix, upgrade window SLOs
Capacity model uses historical token throughput, expected concurrency per customer, and autoscaler headroom (1.5x peak)
Wave 1 focuses on customers with on-prem HA requirements; feature freeze window 48 hours prior to upgrade
Wave 2 expands to VPC customers with explicit burst capacity commitments negotiated in contract
Post-roll evaluation will surface cost delta vs projected and any emergent reliability regressions

risks: Capacity under-provisioning if customer concurrency > modeled assumptions leading to SLA breaches
Delayed KMS/HSM onboarding for customers causing rollout holdouts
Upgrade rollback scenarios not exercised for specific on-prem hardware variants
Cross-team bandwidth constraints during overlapping release windows (Console + Runtime teams)
mitigations: Reserve dedicated pilot slots and run stress tests with 1.5x concurrency within staging
Create a KMS onboarding checklist and pre-flight verification step before enrollment
Add forced rollback rehearsals for each hardware profile during Wave 1 dry run
Coordinate release windows across product teams and block calendar during critical merges
success_metrics: No customer-facing SLA breaches in Wave 1
Capacity cost delta within +/-10% of forecast
Customer onboarding NPS >= 8 for pilot cohort
Number of post-roll issues per 100 customer-days <= 0.5
rollout_waves: Wave 1: Pilot on-prem customers (10 customers) — validate runbooks and rollback — 2025-04-15
Wave 2: Regional VPC expansion (25 customers) — validate autoscaler behavior — 2025-05-15
acceptance_criteria: Governance checklist signed by Security and Legal
Capacity model validated in staging with synthetic and customer traces
Upgrade runbook executed end-to-end with successful rollbacks in two rehearsal runs
Customer onboarding packet delivered and reviewed by CS for Wave 1 customers
